semanticLinks.rationale: Breakfast with definite/indefinite article is one teaching concept. Both historical IDs and exact study cards survive; no learner migration.

sameFormGroups.rationale: Town square versus available place/spot; distinct meanings.
Transport ticket counter versus public-service counter; contextual specialisations, not unrelated lemmas.
Physical opening versus opening a digital file/app; contextual transfer, not a newly discovered root verb.
Clothes fitting versus an arrangement being acceptable; related pragmatic uses.
Preposition after an event versus standalone sequence adverb; preserve grammatical uses.
Spatial endpoint versus temporal endpoint; related uses with separate support.
Transport service/timetable versus work schedule; contextual specialisations.
An item being missing versus missing a bus/event; different constructions.
Professional experience versus an experienced event; related count/mass uses.

vocabulary.example: Bonjour madame, je voudrais un café.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Hello, madam, I would like a coffee.
vocabulary.note: A polite greeting when you arrive.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Good evening, sir!
vocabulary.note: A neutral greeting on arrival in the evening. There is no single fixed switch time for everyone.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Hi, Léa!
vocabulary.note: Informal: use with friends or people you already greet familiarly. It can open or close an exchange.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Goodbye, have a good day!
vocabulary.note: Neutral polite leave-taking; do not use it as a greeting on arrival.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Goodbye, see you soon!
vocabulary.note: A friendly goodbye when you expect or hope to meet again soon; no exact date is specified.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: See you tomorrow, Léa!
vocabulary.note: Use when you expect to see the person the next day.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Thank you, have a good day!
vocabulary.note: A wish when leaving during the day. La journée (feminine) means the day as a period of time.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Goodbye and have a good evening!
vocabulary.note: A wish when leaving for the evening. La soirée (feminine) means the evening as a period of time.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: A coffee, please.
vocabulary.note: Use vous with staff you do not know.
vocabulary.pictureAlt: Two hands together in a polite request

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: One moment, please.
vocabulary.note: Use with one person you already address as tu. Un instant (masculine) means one moment.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Thank you, have a good day!
vocabulary.note: A natural way to thank someone.
vocabulary.pictureAlt: A small thank-you card with a heart

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Thank you very much for your help.
vocabulary.note: Merci pour introduces what you are thanking someone for.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: You’re welcome, have a good day!
vocabulary.note: Common neutral response to merci.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Sorry, I didn’t hear.
vocabulary.note: Use for a small apology. Said as Pardon ? with a questioning voice, it can ask someone to repeat.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Excuse me, I am looking for the exit.
vocabulary.note: Use vous with a stranger; excuse-moi is the familiar form.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Sorry, I’m late.
vocabulary.note: The tu form, for one person you already address familiarly. Keep the hyphen in writing.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Hello, how are you?
vocabulary.note: Uses vous: a polite question to one person, or a question to several people. Learn the whole phrase first.

vocabulary.meaning: how are you? / how’s it going?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Hi, how’s it going?
vocabulary.note: Conversational and often familiar; comment allez-vous ? is a useful polite starting point with strangers.

vocabulary.meaning: I’m well / things are going well
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I’m well, thank you.
vocabulary.note: A short conversational response; learn ça va bien as a whole phrase to answer a check-in.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Very well, thank you. And you?
vocabulary.note: A complete short response; you do not need to add je (I).

vocabulary.example: Pas très bien, je suis fatiguée.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Not very well, I’m tired.
vocabulary.note: An honest short response. Fatiguée is the feminine form of tired; fatigué is masculine.

vocabulary.example: Ça va bien, merci. Et vous ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I’m well, thank you. And you?
vocabulary.note: Return the question with vous to an adult you address politely, or to several people.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Very well, thank you. And you?
vocabulary.note: Return the question to one person you already address as tu. Toi is the form used after et here.

vocabulary.example: À tout à l’heure, à midi !
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: See you later, at noon!
vocabulary.note: Use when you expect to meet again later the same day. For tomorrow, use à demain.

vocabulary.example: Je ne comprends pas cette phrase.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I do not understand this sentence.
vocabulary.note: Useful as a complete phrase; ne is often omitted in casual speech.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Can you repeat the number?
vocabulary.note: Polite everyday spoken question with vous.

vocabulary.example: Parlez plus lentement, s’il vous plaît.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Please speak more slowly.
vocabulary.note: Plus lentement asks for a slower pace, without asking someone to shout.

vocabulary.example: Le nom, encore une fois, s’il vous plaît.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The name one more time, please.
vocabulary.note: A short repair phrase; keep a polite tone.

vocabulary.example: Ce mot, ça veut dire quoi ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: What does this word mean?
vocabulary.note: Everyday spoken question; que veut dire ce mot ? is more formal.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Thank you, I understand now.
vocabulary.note: Learn as a useful chunk before studying the past tense.

vocabulary.example: Vous pouvez m’aider avec ce mot ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Can you help me with this word?
vocabulary.note: M’ means me before a vowel.

vocabulary.example: Un instant, je cherche mon téléphone.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: One moment, I am looking for my phone.
vocabulary.note: Un instant is masculine; useful as a short request.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Yes, I speak English.
vocabulary.note: Neutral affirmative answer.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: No, thank you, no coffee.
vocabulary.note: Add merci for a polite refusal.

vocabulary.example: Je ne parle pas encore bien français.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I do not speak French well yet.
vocabulary.note: Use for something that has not happened or developed yet.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I do not live here anymore.
vocabulary.note: Put ne before the verb and plus after it; ne becomes n’ before a vowel.

vocabulary.example: Je ne peux pas venir ce soir.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I cannot come this evening.
vocabulary.note: Add a verb in its dictionary form: venir, lire, parler.

vocabulary.meaning: I do not have any / a
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I do not have a pen.
vocabulary.note: After not having, un/une/des usually becomes de.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Where do you live?
vocabulary.note: Où has an accent; ou without it means or.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: When are you arriving?
vocabulary.note: A time question; a rising voice is natural here.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: How does it work?
vocabulary.note: Can ask about a method or how something works.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: What language do you speak?
vocabulary.note: Quel with a masculine noun, quelle with a feminine noun.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Do you speak English?
vocabulary.note: Introduces a yes/no question; no separate meaning in English.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Can I come in?
vocabulary.note: Useful for asking permission; follow peux with a verb.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Can you write down the name?
vocabulary.note: L’ means it; a practical request for an unfamiliar word.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Can you spell out your name?
vocabulary.note: Vous pouvez épeler ? is a polite spoken request. J’épelle means I spell out.

vocabulary.example: Vous pouvez me montrer la page ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Can you show me the page?
vocabulary.note: Me montrer means show me.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Do you have a simple example?
vocabulary.note: Masculine even though it ends in e.

vocabulary.example: Dix heures demain, c’est bien ça ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Ten o’clock tomorrow, is that right?
vocabulary.note: Use to check information you have just heard.

vocabulary.example: Comment on dit « hello » en français ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: How do you say “hello” in French?
vocabulary.note: Language names have no article after en.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: There are no places left.
vocabulary.note: Number; useful when reading a counter or a balance.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: One person is waiting.
vocabulary.note: Un before a masculine noun; une before a feminine noun.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: There are two of us.
vocabulary.note: Number; unchanged before masculine or feminine nouns.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I have three appointments this week.
vocabulary.note: Number; the final s is usually silent.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: There are four chairs.
vocabulary.note: Number; no plural s on the number itself.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I will arrive in five minutes.
vocabulary.note: Number; final consonant pronunciation varies with the following word.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: My code ends in six.
vocabulary.note: Its final sound changes in connected speech.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The number is seven.
vocabulary.note: The p is silent; the final t is heard.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: We need eight chairs.
vocabulary.note: Do not pronounce an English h.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: There are nine tickets left.
vocabulary.note: Here neuf is a number, not the adjective new.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The journey takes ten minutes.
vocabulary.note: Number; dix minutes has a silent final x.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: There are eleven of us.
vocabulary.note: Learn as a whole number.

vocabulary.example: Il y a douze œufs dans la boîte.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: There are twelve eggs in the box.
vocabulary.note: A dozen is une douzaine.

vocabulary.example: Le total est de treize euros.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The total is thirteen euros.
vocabulary.note: Do not confuse treize with trente, thirty.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: There are fourteen minutes left.
vocabulary.note: Learn as one word.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: It costs fifteen euros.
vocabulary.note: Do not confuse quinze with cinquante, fifty.

vocabulary.example: La réunion est à seize heures.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The meeting is at four p.m.
vocabulary.note: Sixteen hours in the 24-hour clock is four p.m.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The ticket costs seventeen euros.
vocabulary.note: From seventeen, combine dix with another number.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: There are eighteen places left.
vocabulary.note: Combine dix and huit.

vocabulary.example: Le total est de dix-neuf euros.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The total is nineteen euros.
vocabulary.note: Combine dix and neuf.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Here are twenty euros.
vocabulary.note: The final t is normally silent when vingt stands alone.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The ticket costs thirty euros.
vocabulary.note: Trente et un is thirty-one.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The bag costs forty euros.
vocabulary.note: Compare quarante with quatorze, fourteen.

vocabulary.example: Ça fait cinquante euros en tout.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: That is fifty euros altogether.
vocabulary.note: Compare cinquante with quinze, fifteen.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: There are sixty of us.
vocabulary.note: Metropolitan French uses soixante-dix for seventy.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The coat costs seventy euros.
vocabulary.note: Literally sixty-ten in metropolitan French.

vocabulary.example: Le total est de quatre-vingts euros.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The total is eighty euros.
vocabulary.note: Keep s for exactly eighty; no s before another number: quatre-vingt-deux.

vocabulary.example: La facture est de quatre-vingt-dix euros.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The bill is ninety euros.
vocabulary.note: Literally eighty-ten; vingt has no s before dix.

vocabulary.example: Le total est de cent euros.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The total is a hundred euros.
vocabulary.note: Cent is invariable here; deux cents has s when no other number follows.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: How many of you are there?
vocabulary.note: Combien de + noun: combien de personnes ?

vocabulary.meaning: to be called / have as a name
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: My name is Alex.
vocabulary.note: Reflexive verb; je m’appelle, vous vous appelez.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: My first name is Alex.
vocabulary.note: Distinct from nom de famille.

vocabulary.example: Mon nom de famille, c’est Martin.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: My surname is Martin.
vocabulary.note: Formal contexts often ask for nom and prénom.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Pleased to meet you; my name is Paul.
vocabulary.note: Enchantée for a feminine speaker in writing; same pronunciation.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I live in Nantes.
vocabulary.note: Regular -er verb; use à before a city.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I come from London.
vocabulary.note: Here origin, not the recent-past pattern venir de + infinitive.

vocabulary.example: Nantes est une ville en France.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Nantes is a city in France.
vocabulary.note: French does not always distinguish town and city here.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Which country do you come from?
vocabulary.note: Final s is silent.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Which language do you speak?
vocabulary.note: Plural langues for more than one.

vocabulary.example: Je parle anglais et un peu français.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I speak English and a little French.
vocabulary.note: Regular -er verb; no article in parler anglais.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: This is my friend Paul.
vocabulary.note: Une amie for a woman.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: My neighbour is called Léa.
vocabulary.note: Un voisin for a man.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: My family lives in London.
vocabulary.note: Singular family takes a singular verb.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I have one child.
vocabulary.note: Un enfant is the general form; une enfant can specify a girl.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: My brother lives near here.
vocabulary.note: Keep the grave accent.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: My sister speaks French.
vocabulary.note: The ligature œ is standard; soeur is common when typing.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The class starts on Monday.
vocabulary.note: Day names have no capital letter in ordinary French. Le lundi means on Mondays.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The class is on Tuesday.
vocabulary.note: No on before a specific weekday in French.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: On Wednesday, I am working.
vocabulary.note: Le mercredi means on Wednesdays as a regular habit.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Are you free on Thursday?
vocabulary.note: A specific day uses no article here.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: See you on Friday.
vocabulary.note: On se voit is a familiar way to arrange seeing someone.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Which day suits you?
vocabulary.note: Jour is masculine; therefore quel.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I work on Saturdays.
vocabulary.note: No article for a particular coming Saturday; le samedi for a regular habit.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am staying at home on Sunday.
vocabulary.note: Le dimanche can describe a weekly habit.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Today is Monday.
vocabulary.note: Time word with an apostrophe; no article.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: It’s for tomorrow morning.
vocabulary.note: Time word; no article is needed.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Yesterday, I worked.
vocabulary.note: The example uses a past-tense chunk; the target is the time word.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am free this week.
vocabulary.note: Cette semaine means this week.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The class starts in January.
vocabulary.note: Use en before a month.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am coming in February.
vocabulary.note: Keep the accent on é.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: My birthday is in March.
vocabulary.note: The final s is pronounced.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: We are leaving in April.
vocabulary.note: French month names have lower-case initials.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The visit is in May.
vocabulary.note: No English y in the spelling.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am working here in June.
vocabulary.note: Distinguish juin from juillet, July.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The festival is in July.
vocabulary.note: Not juin, which is June.

vocabulary.example: Je suis en vacances en août.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am on holiday in August.
vocabulary.note: Pronounced /u/ or /ut/. Août is the traditional spelling; aout is also accepted.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The class resumes in September.
vocabulary.note: No capital letter in French.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am moving house in October.
vocabulary.note: Use en for in October.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: My family is coming in November.
vocabulary.note: Use en before the month.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The party is in December.
vocabulary.note: Keep the accent on é.

vocabulary.example: Je me réveille à sept heures.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I wake up at seven o’clock.
vocabulary.note: Se réveiller is waking up; se lever is getting out of bed. With je, use me.

vocabulary.example: Je m’habille avant le petit déjeuner.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I get dressed before breakfast.
vocabulary.note: Se becomes s’ before a vowel sound; with je say je m’habille.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I brush my teeth.
vocabulary.note: Use les dents with the reflexive pronoun: je me brosse les dents. Une dent is feminine.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I have to hurry.
vocabulary.note: After dois, keep the verb in its dictionary form but match the pronoun to je: me dépêcher.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am ready to leave.
vocabulary.note: A feminine speaker writes prête. Être prêt à + a verb means to be ready to do something.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I arrive at work on time.
vocabulary.note: This means at the expected time. En retard means late. Une heure is feminine.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: It is one o’clock.
vocabulary.note: For clock time, use il est.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I will arrive in a minute.
vocabulary.note: Dans gives time from now.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: We eat at noon.
vocabulary.note: Used without an article in à midi.

vocabulary.example: Le dernier bus part à minuit.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The last bus leaves at midnight.
vocabulary.note: Used without an article in à minuit.

vocabulary.example: Il est huit heures et demie.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: It is half past eight.
vocabulary.note: Demie agrees with feminine heure; midi et demi and minuit et demi have no final e.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I come home in the evening.
vocabulary.note: Ce soir means this evening or tonight.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I walk every day.
vocabulary.note: A frequency phrase: tous les jours. Do not add a preposition before it.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Which day are you available?
vocabulary.note: Here a day of the week.

vocabulary.meaning: on weekdays / during the working week
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I leave early on weekdays.
vocabulary.note: Contrasts with le week-end. This is a time phrase, not a claim that everyone works Monday to Friday.

vocabulary.example: Le week-end, je me lève tard.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: At the weekend, I get up late.
vocabulary.note: Un week-end is masculine. Here le week-end describes a usual routine.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I go to bed early.
vocabulary.note: An adverb with a circumflex; no gender ending. Plus tôt means earlier.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I come home late on Fridays.
vocabulary.note: Tard describes a late time; en retard means late compared with an expected time.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I live on Rue des Lilas.
vocabulary.note: The street name in this original example is fictional.

vocabulary.example: On se retrouve sur la place.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: We are meeting in the square.
vocabulary.note: Here an open public square, not a seat.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Turn at the crossroads.
vocabulary.note: A meeting point of streets.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Cross the bridge.
Turn after the traffic light.
vocabulary.note: Here a traffic signal; plural feux.

vocabulary.example: Le passage piéton est devant vous.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The pedestrian crossing is in front of you.
vocabulary.note: Also called a passage pour piétons.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Where is the post office?
vocabulary.note: A polite neutral way to ask for a location.

vocabulary.example: La banque est à côté du café.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The bank is next to the café.
vocabulary.note: De + le becomes du.

vocabulary.example: La poste est en face de la mairie.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The post office is opposite the town hall.
vocabulary.note: Keep de before the landmark.

vocabulary.example: La porte est entre les deux fenêtres.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The door is between the two windows.
vocabulary.note: Entre… et… joins two different landmarks.

vocabulary.example: Le jardin est derrière la mairie.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The garden is behind the town hall.
vocabulary.note: No de is needed after derrière.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am waiting in front of the bank.
vocabulary.note: Devant is in front of; en face de is opposite.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Go straight on as far as the bridge.
vocabulary.note: Do not confuse droit here with à droite, to the right.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Turn left at the traffic light.
vocabulary.note: Tournez is the vous instruction form.

vocabulary.example: Tournez à droite après la banque.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Turn right after the bank.
vocabulary.note: À droite means to the right.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Cross the square.
vocabulary.note: Regular -er verb; follow pedestrian signals when walking.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Continue as far as the crossroads.
vocabulary.note: Jusqu’à means as far as / until.

vocabulary.example: Prenez la première rue à gauche.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Take the first street on the left.
vocabulary.note: Première agrees with feminine rue.

vocabulary.example: La mairie est sur cette place.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The town hall is on this square.
vocabulary.note: Vocabulary for a place, not advice about any particular procedure.

vocabulary.example: Où est le bureau de poste ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Where is the post office?
vocabulary.note: La poste can mean the postal service.

vocabulary.example: Il y a une banque près du pont.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: There is a bank near the bridge.

vocabulary.example: La bibliothèque est derrière la mairie.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The library is behind the town hall.
vocabulary.note: A library lends books; a bookshop is une librairie.

vocabulary.example: Le supermarché est au bout de la rue.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The supermarket is at the end of the street.
Where is the police station?
vocabulary.note: A place name for asking directions; other police services have different names.

vocabulary.example: Je prends le bus pour aller au travail.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I take the bus to get to work.
vocabulary.note: Pronounce the final s.

vocabulary.example: On va au centre en métro.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: We’re going to the centre by metro.

vocabulary.example: Je prends le bus pour aller au travail.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I take the bus to get to work.
vocabulary.note: Infinitive prendre; je prends.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Does this train go to Lyon?

vocabulary.example: Je vais au travail à vélo.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I go to work by bicycle.
vocabulary.note: Use à vélo.

vocabulary.example: La gare est à dix minutes à pied.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The station is a ten-minute walk away.
vocabulary.note: Travel phrase. Pied stays singular in à pied.

vocabulary.example: Le tramway arrive dans deux minutes.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The tram is arriving in two minutes.
vocabulary.note: Tram is a common shorter form.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Where is the bus stop?
vocabulary.note: Here a place where a bus or tram stops.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I get on the bus.
vocabulary.note: Monter dans le train or dans le bus; dans introduces the vehicle.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I’m looking for the railway station.

vocabulary.example: Notre train part de quel quai ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Which platform does our train leave from?
vocabulary.note: Check the actual platform or track signs.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I take line two.

vocabulary.example: Prenez la ligne deux, direction Nation.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Take line two towards Nation.
vocabulary.note: Travel phrase used without an article before the destination.

vocabulary.example: Où est la station de métro ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Where is the metro station?
vocabulary.note: Station is used for metro stops.

vocabulary.example: Un billet pour Lille, s’il vous plaît.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: A ticket to Lille, please.
vocabulary.note: Common for rail journeys.

vocabulary.meaning: a single ticket; a one-way journey
vocabulary.example: Je voudrais un aller simple pour Lille.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I would like a single ticket to Lille.

vocabulary.meaning: a return ticket; a round trip
vocabulary.example: Un aller-retour pour Lyon, s’il vous plaît.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: A return ticket to Lyon, please.

vocabulary.example: Je peux acheter mon billet au distributeur ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Can I buy my ticket at the machine?
vocabulary.note: Here a ticket machine; the context matters.

vocabulary.example: Je voudrais acheter un billet pour Lille.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I would like to buy a ticket to Lille.
vocabulary.note: A useful infinitive phrase after voudrais.

vocabulary.meaning: to validate a travel ticket or pass
vocabulary.example: Je dois valider mon billet ici ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Do I need to validate my ticket here?
vocabulary.note: Infinitive verb. Ask staff: validation arrangements vary by network and ticket.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Is the ticket counter open?
vocabulary.note: Final t is silent.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: A baguette, please.
vocabulary.note: Bien cuite asks for a darker, well-baked crust.
vocabulary.pictureAlt: A long baguette with diagonal cuts

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I’ll have two croissants.

vocabulary.example: Vous avez un sac pour le pain ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Do you have a bag for the bread?
vocabulary.pictureAlt: A paper shopping bag with handles

vocabulary.example: Un pain de campagne, s’il vous plaît.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: A country-style loaf, please.
vocabulary.note: A style of bread, not a guarantee of particular ingredients.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Do you have wholemeal bread?
vocabulary.note: Du is for an unspecified amount.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Which bread is well baked?
vocabulary.note: Quel agrees with masculine singular pain.

vocabulary.example: Je voudrais quatre tranches de ce pain.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I would like four slices of this bread.
vocabulary.note: De introduces what is sliced.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I would like this bread sliced.
vocabulary.note: Adjective agreeing with pain, masculine singular; feminine tranchée.

vocabulary.example: Je préfère un pain bien cuit.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I prefer a well-baked loaf.
vocabulary.note: Adjective phrase; feminine bien cuite. In a bakery this asks for a darker bake.

vocabulary.example: Deux pains au chocolat, s’il vous plaît.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Two chocolate-filled pastries, please.
vocabulary.note: Chocolatine is a regional name, notably in southwestern France.

vocabulary.example: Cette brioche est pour deux personnes ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Is this brioche for two people?
vocabulary.note: A rich, soft bread.

vocabulary.example: Vous avez des chaussons aux pommes ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Do you have apple turnovers?
vocabulary.note: Aux pommes means with apple in this pastry name.

vocabulary.example: Je prends une tartelette aux fraises.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I’ll have a strawberry tartlet.

vocabulary.example: Et avec ça, vous voulez une brioche ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Would you like a brioche as well?
vocabulary.note: A common question from shop staff; literally and with that?

vocabulary.example: Ces chaussons aux pommes, j’en prends deux.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I’ll have two of these apple turnovers.
vocabulary.note: En refers back to the item; pronounce j’en as one linked unit.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I’ll take three apples.
I need three apples.
vocabulary.note: Useful fixed chunk. Il does not mean a particular person here.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I would like four tomatoes.
I need two carrots.
vocabulary.note: One r and double t.

vocabulary.example: Vous avez des pommes de terre ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Do you have potatoes?
vocabulary.note: Keep de terre when naming a potato.

vocabulary.example: Un kilo de tomates, s’il vous plaît.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: A kilogram of tomatoes, please.
vocabulary.note: Everyday short form of kilogramme.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I’ll take two bananas.
I need some rice.
vocabulary.note: Final z is silent.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Where is the pasta?
vocabulary.note: Usually plural in this food sense. Keep the accent.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I’m looking for some flour.
I’m going to buy some rice.
vocabulary.note: Infinitive after vais. Present: j’achète.

vocabulary.example: Il me faut de l’huile d’olive.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I need some olive oil.
vocabulary.note: De la becomes de l’ before a vowel sound.

vocabulary.example: Je prends un paquet de pâtes.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I’ll take a packet of pasta.
vocabulary.note: Final t is silent.

vocabulary.example: Je cherche du sucre pour mon café.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I’m looking for some sugar for my coffee.
I would like some unsalted butter.
vocabulary.note: Beurre doux means unsalted butter.

vocabulary.example: Je prends un morceau de ce fromage.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I’ll take a piece of this cheese.
I’m looking for plain yogurts.
vocabulary.note: Nature here means plain.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: How much does this cheese cost?
vocabulary.note: Everyday spoken question. ça needs a cedilla.

vocabulary.example: Quatre tranches de jambon, s’il vous plaît.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Four slices of ham, please.

vocabulary.example: Quel est le prix de ce fromage ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: What is the price of this cheese?
vocabulary.note: Same written form in singular and plural.

vocabulary.example: Vous avez de la crème fraîche ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Do you have crème fraîche?

vocabulary.example: Je voudrais un café, s’il vous plaît.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I would like a coffee, please.
vocabulary.note: In France, un café usually means an espresso.
vocabulary.pictureAlt: A small cup of coffee on a saucer

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Some water, please.
vocabulary.note: De l’ introduces an unspecified amount before a vowel.
vocabulary.pictureAlt: A glass and a jug of water

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The menu, please.
vocabulary.note: At a restaurant, la carte lists the individual dishes.
vocabulary.pictureAlt: An open restaurant menu with food symbols

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The bill, please.
vocabulary.note: La becomes l’ before a vowel.

vocabulary.example: Vous avez une table pour deux ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Do you have a table for two?
vocabulary.note: A useful request when you arrive.

vocabulary.example: Je voudrais réserver une table pour samedi.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I would like to book a table for Saturday.
vocabulary.note: Verb phrase. Use réserver + the thing you want to book.

vocabulary.example: J’ai une réservation pour ce soir.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I have a reservation for this evening.
Can we eat in the outdoor seating area?
vocabulary.note: En terrasse means in the outdoor seating area.

vocabulary.example: Une table pour deux, s’il vous plaît.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: A table for two, please.
vocabulary.note: Short practical phrase; deux has no final pronounced x.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Can we eat inside?
vocabulary.note: Location phrase.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: There are three of us.
vocabulary.note: Used for anyone, regardless of gender.

vocabulary.example: Je prends une entrée et un plat.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I’ll have a starter and a main course.
vocabulary.note: In France an entrée is a starter, before the main course.

vocabulary.example: Quel est le plat du jour ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: What is the dish of the day?
vocabulary.note: Here plat means a dish or main course.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Would you like a dessert?
vocabulary.note: Pronounce the ss like s in see.

vocabulary.example: Le menu comprend une entrée et un plat.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The set meal includes a starter and a main course.
vocabulary.note: Often a set combination at one price; la carte is the list of individual dishes.

vocabulary.example: Je prends le plat du jour.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I’ll have the dish of the day.
vocabulary.note: In an ordering situation, prendre means to have or choose.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Do you have a vegetarian dish?
vocabulary.note: Adjective: végétarien with a masculine noun, végétarienne with a feminine noun.

vocabulary.example: Je prends du poulet avec des légumes.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I’ll have chicken with vegetables.
vocabulary.note: Du is used for an unspecified amount of food.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I’m looking for a pair of black trousers.
vocabulary.note: Singular in French; trousers is plural in English.

vocabulary.example: Vous avez cette chemise en bleu ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Do you have this shirt in blue?
I would like a white T-shirt.
vocabulary.note: T-shirt is another common spelling.

vocabulary.example: Cette robe existe en taille quarante ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Does this dress come in size forty?
I’ll take this blue jumper.
vocabulary.note: Everyday word for a knitted top.

vocabulary.example: Je cherche le rayon des surgelés.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I’m looking for the frozen-food section.
vocabulary.note: Use chercher + the thing sought; no pour.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I’m looking for a warm coat.
vocabulary.note: Plural: des manteaux.

vocabulary.meaning: a pair of shoes; some shoes
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I’m looking for comfortable shoes.
vocabulary.note: Usually plural for a pair.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: These trainers are light.
vocabulary.note: Usually plural for a pair.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I would like some black socks.
This scarf is very soft.
This belt is too long.

vocabulary.example: Je porte ces chaussures au travail.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I wear these shoes at work.
vocabulary.note: Here porter means wear, rather than carry.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I would like to try on this hat.
vocabulary.note: Plural: des chapeaux.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Do you have the next size up?
vocabulary.note: Use pointure for shoe size.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: What shoe size do you take?
vocabulary.note: Specifically footwear size.

vocabulary.example: Vous avez ce pull dans une autre couleur ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Do you have this jumper in another colour?
vocabulary.note: Useful question ending after naming an item.

vocabulary.example: Je voudrais ce pantalon en noir.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I would like these trousers in black.
vocabulary.note: Adjective: noir, noire, noirs, noires.

vocabulary.example: Vous avez ce pull en bleu ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Do you have this jumper in blue?
vocabulary.note: Adjective: bleu, bleue, bleus, bleues.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: This jumper is too small.
vocabulary.note: Adjective phrase; feminine trop petite. Trop means too, beyond what is wanted.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Which colour do you prefer?
I live in a small flat.
The kitchen is on the left.
vocabulary.note: Here a room, not cooking or cuisine as a style.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: There are two bedrooms.

vocabulary.example: La salle de bains est à droite.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The bathroom is on the right.
vocabulary.note: It does not necessarily contain a toilet.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Where is the toilet?
vocabulary.note: Plural even for one toilet room.

vocabulary.example: Le salon est à côté de la cuisine.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The living room is next to the kitchen.

vocabulary.example: On peut mettre le lit ici ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Can we put the bed here?
vocabulary.note: Final t is silent.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: A chair is missing.

vocabulary.example: Le canapé est dans le salon.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The sofa is in the living room.

vocabulary.example: On peut mettre le lit ici ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Can we put the bed here?
vocabulary.note: Here mettre means put; je mets, on met.

vocabulary.example: Le réfrigérateur est dans la cuisine.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The refrigerator is in the kitchen.
vocabulary.note: Frigo is a common informal alternative.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Is there a washing machine?

vocabulary.example: Il y a une armoire dans la chambre.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: There is a wardrobe in the bedroom.
This key opens the door.
vocabulary.note: Clef is another accepted spelling.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The door is closed.
Which floor is the flat on?
vocabulary.note: French étage numbering starts above the ground floor.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The lift is on the left.
This key opens the door.
vocabulary.note: Infinitive ouvrir; present form ouvre.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I live on the ground floor.
vocabulary.note: Au combines à and le.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The staircase is behind this door.
vocabulary.note: Singular when referring to one staircase.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I like listening to music.
vocabulary.note: With an activity, often means like; with a person, can mean love.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I read on the train.
vocabulary.note: Irregular verb; je lis, nous lisons.

vocabulary.example: J’écoute de la musique le soir.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I listen to music in the evening.
vocabulary.note: Écouter takes a direct object, without à.

vocabulary.example: On regarde un film chez moi ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Shall we watch a film at my place?
vocabulary.note: Informal suggestion with on between friends.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I like gardening on Sundays.
vocabulary.note: Regular -er verb; can stand without an object.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I draw in a sketchbook.
vocabulary.note: Regular -er verb; a leisure activity here.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The weather is nice today.
vocabulary.note: Weather expression with impersonal il; beau does not describe a person here.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: It is hot this afternoon.
vocabulary.note: Use il fait chaud for weather; j’ai chaud means I feel hot.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: It is cold this morning.
vocabulary.note: Use il fait froid for weather; j’ai froid means I feel cold.

vocabulary.example: Il pleut, je prends mon manteau.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: It is raining; I am taking my coat.
vocabulary.note: Present weather expression from pleuvoir; do not say il fait pleut.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: It is sunny.
vocabulary.note: Du soleil means sunshine in this weather phrase.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: It is windy.
vocabulary.note: French commonly uses il y a du vent.

vocabulary.example: Je fais du sport le samedi.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I exercise on Saturdays.
vocabulary.note: Faire du sport is the usual general expression.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: We can walk to the park.
vocabulary.note: Regular -er verb; here moving on foot, not a device working.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I run in the park.
vocabulary.note: Irregular verb; je cours, nous courons.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I like swimming in the morning.
vocabulary.note: Regular -er verb with nous nageons.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The swimming pool is open on Sunday.
vocabulary.note: A venue, not a swimming activity.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I would like to invite you to dinner.
vocabulary.note: Regular -er verb; t’ is familiar you before a vowel.

vocabulary.meaning: would you like to? / do you fancy it?
vocabulary.example: Un café samedi, ça te dit ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Would you like a coffee on Saturday?
vocabulary.note: Informal spoken invitation between people using tu; ça vous dit ? with vous.

vocabulary.example: Tu veux venir chez moi samedi ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Do you want to come to my place on Saturday?
vocabulary.note: Chez moi means at/to my home.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Can you bring a fork?
vocabulary.note: Use after pouvez in a request.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Thank you for your invitation.

vocabulary.example: On prépare un dîner pour quatre.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: We are preparing dinner for four.
vocabulary.note: Also a verb: dîner, to have dinner.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Yes, gladly!
vocabulary.note: Warm, neutral way to accept an invitation.

vocabulary.example: Samedi à huit heures, ça me va.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Saturday at eight works for me.
vocabulary.note: Here agreement with a plan, not clothing fit.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I would be happy to come with you.
vocabulary.note: An adverb; no gender ending.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am free on Friday evening.
vocabulary.note: Libre has the same form for masculine and feminine.

vocabulary.example: Il reste une place pour moi ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Is there a place left for me?
vocabulary.note: Here room for one person, not a town square.

vocabulary.example: Je peux me joindre à vous ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Can I join you?
vocabulary.note: With je, se becomes me; retain à.

vocabulary.example: Désolé, je ne peux pas venir samedi.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Sorry, I cannot come on Saturday.
vocabulary.note: Désolée for a feminine speaker; keep the refusal clear.

vocabulary.example: Vendredi, ce n’est pas possible pour moi.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Friday is not possible for me.
vocabulary.note: A neutral way to state a constraint.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am busy on Saturday.
vocabulary.note: Adjective: occupée for a feminine speaker.

vocabulary.example: On peut se voir une autre fois.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: We can meet another time.
vocabulary.note: Useful when postponing an invitation; fois means time or occasion here.

vocabulary.example: Je dois partir à huit heures.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I have to leave at eight.
vocabulary.note: Dois + dictionary verb expresses a necessity.

vocabulary.example: Je ne peux pas venir, mais merci quand même.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I cannot come, but thank you anyway.
vocabulary.note: Use a warm tone so it sounds appreciative.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I would like an appointment.
vocabulary.note: The spelling is unchanged in the plural.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am looking for a doctor.
vocabulary.note: Une médecin is also used for a woman.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am available on Thursday.
vocabulary.note: Adjective; the same form for masculine and feminine.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I prefer the morning.
vocabulary.note: Le matin can also mean in the mornings.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I would like to make an appointment.
vocabulary.note: No article inside prendre rendez-vous. Je voudrais prendre rendez-vous is a polite request.

vocabulary.meaning: to be in pain / to hurt
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: It hurts here.
vocabulary.note: Use avoir mal à plus the body part. This is a language pattern, not a diagnosis.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I have a headache.
vocabulary.note: À la stays separate.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: My stomach hurts.
vocabulary.note: Everyday word for the abdominal area.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: My back hurts.
vocabulary.note: The final s is silent.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I have a fever.
vocabulary.note: French uses de la in this expression.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am very tired today.
vocabulary.note: Adjective: fatiguée for a feminine speaker; not a medical diagnosis.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am looking for a pharmacy.
vocabulary.note: Use vous when addressing staff.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Here is my prescription.
vocabulary.note: Possessive mon before a vowel even with a feminine noun.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: What is this medicine called?
vocabulary.note: Ask a professional about use, rather than guessing.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I have an allergy to eggs.
vocabulary.note: State a real allergy clearly and check with staff.

vocabulary.example: Je ne comprends pas la notice.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I do not understand the leaflet.
vocabulary.note: Here the information leaflet supplied with a medicine.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Can you explain this sentence?
vocabulary.note: Regular -er verb; polite spoken request with vous.

vocabulary.example: Je coupe les légumes sur la planche à découper.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I cut the vegetables on the chopping board.
vocabulary.note: Learn the whole noun phrase.

vocabulary.example: Je mets les légumes dans un bol.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I put the vegetables in a bowl.

vocabulary.example: Tu peux me passer une cuillère ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Can you pass me a spoon?
vocabulary.note: Cuiller is another accepted spelling.

vocabulary.example: La balance est sur la table.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The kitchen scales are on the table.
vocabulary.note: Singular in French. Here a device for weighing ingredients.

vocabulary.example: Je me lave les mains avant de cuisiner.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I wash my hands before cooking.
vocabulary.note: Je me lave; tu te laves. Use les mains rather than mes mains in this expression.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I clean the table.
vocabulary.note: Infinitive nettoyer; present je nettoie.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I cut an onion.
vocabulary.note: The usual pronunciation begins with an o sound, without a separate i sound.

vocabulary.example: J’ajoute de l’ail dans la soupe.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I add some garlic to the soup.
vocabulary.note: Masculine despite the elided article. Une gousse d’ail is one clove.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I wash a courgette.
Can you wash the courgettes?
vocabulary.note: Laver + a thing; se laver for washing yourself.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I peel the potatoes.
vocabulary.note: Use directly before the food being peeled.

vocabulary.example: Je coupe les courgettes en petits morceaux.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I cut the courgettes into small pieces.
vocabulary.note: En morceaux means into pieces.

vocabulary.example: Cette recette est pour quatre personnes.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: This recipe is for four people.
I add a little salt.
vocabulary.note: Du is for an unspecified amount; un peu de sel means a little salt.

vocabulary.example: Tu veux du poivre dans la soupe ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Do you want some pepper in the soup?
vocabulary.note: Black or white pepper, rather than a vegetable pepper.

vocabulary.example: J’ajoute le sel, puis je mélange.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I add the salt, then I mix.
vocabulary.note: Recipe instructions often use the infinitive ajouter or the command ajoutez.

vocabulary.example: Je mélange les légumes avec une cuillère.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I mix the vegetables with a spoon.
vocabulary.note: Je mélange; nous mélangeons.

vocabulary.example: Je mets un peu de poivre.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I put in a little pepper.
vocabulary.note: De becomes d’ before a vowel: un peu d’huile.

vocabulary.example: Mon téléphone est dans mon sac.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: My phone is in my bag.
vocabulary.note: Un portable is a common word for a mobile phone.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am waiting for a call.
vocabulary.note: Appeler is the verb.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Can I call you tomorrow?
vocabulary.note: Appeler quelqu’un: no à before the person.

vocabulary.meaning: to answer / pick up the phone
vocabulary.example: Je ne peux pas décrocher maintenant.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I cannot answer the phone now.
vocabulary.note: Here the action of answering a call.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I need to hang up, speak soon.
vocabulary.note: A polite explanation before ending a call.

vocabulary.example: Vous pouvez laisser un message sur ma messagerie vocale.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: You can leave a message on my voicemail.
What is your email address?
vocabulary.note: Adresse électronique is a more formal equivalent.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am sending you an email.
vocabulary.note: Un courriel and un e-mail are also used.

vocabulary.example: Après mon prénom, il y a une arobase.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: After my first name, there is an at sign.
vocabulary.note: Used when dictating an email address.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: It is lea dot martin.
vocabulary.note: Here punctuation in an address.

vocabulary.example: Il y a un tiret entre les deux noms.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: There is a hyphen between the two names.
vocabulary.note: Tiret du milieu makes a hyphen explicit.

vocabulary.example: Écrivez lea, un tiret du bas, puis martin.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Write lea, an underscore, then martin.
vocabulary.note: Everyday way to dictate the _ character.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I have a message for you.
vocabulary.note: Can refer to a written or spoken message.

vocabulary.example: Envoyez-moi un SMS, s’il vous plaît.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Please send me a text message.
vocabulary.note: Say the three letter names; un texto is also common.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am going to send this document.
vocabulary.note: Use envoyer after vais; j’envoie means I send.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am replying to your message.
vocabulary.note: Répondre à quelqu’un / à un message.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I receive your messages.
vocabulary.note: Useful past chunk: j’ai reçu, I received.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Can you forward this email?
vocabulary.note: Here forward a message to another person.

vocabulary.example: Je cherche un hôtel près de la gare.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I’m looking for a hotel near the station.
vocabulary.note: The h is silent: l’hôtel.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I’m staying for one night.
vocabulary.note: Used to count nights of accommodation.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I would like a double room.
vocabulary.note: Ask about beds if it matters; room labels do not guarantee a particular bed arrangement.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Do you have a single room?
vocabulary.note: A room intended for one person.

vocabulary.example: Je voudrais réserver une chambre pour samedi.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I would like to book a room for Saturday.
vocabulary.note: Recycles réserver from Restaurant with a different object.

vocabulary.example: Une chambre pour deux nuits, s’il vous plaît.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: A room for two nights, please.
vocabulary.note: Use plural nuits after deux.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Reception is at the entrance.
vocabulary.note: Here the hotel desk, not a celebration.

vocabulary.example: Votre réservation est à quel nom ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Under what name is your reservation?
vocabulary.note: Staff ask for the name on the booking. Reply au nom de + name.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Here is my passport.
vocabulary.note: Final t is silent.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Do you have an identity document?
vocabulary.note: This is a language example, not a universal document requirement.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Can you fill in this form?
vocabulary.note: Remplir + a form or document; no preposition.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Do I need to sign here?
vocabulary.note: Infinitive after dois. Present: je signe.

vocabulary.example: Le petit déjeuner est à quelle heure ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: What time is breakfast?
vocabulary.note: Also written petit-déjeuner.

vocabulary.example: Il y a une connexion Wi-Fi dans la chambre ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Is there a Wi-Fi connection in the room?

vocabulary.example: Je ne connais pas le mot de passe.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I do not know the password.
vocabulary.note: Only fictional practice details are needed.

vocabulary.example: Le linge de lit est compris ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Is bed linen included?
vocabulary.note: Collective singular noun.

vocabulary.example: Je peux avoir une serviette de bain ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Can I have a bath towel?
vocabulary.note: De bain identifies a towel; une serviette at a restaurant is a napkin.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Is breakfast included?
vocabulary.note: Ask about a named service. Included services vary by booking.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Can I enrol here?
vocabulary.note: S’inscrire is the related verb to enrol.

vocabulary.example: Je voudrais m’inscrire à un cours.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I would like to enrol on a course.
vocabulary.note: S’inscrire à + a course. Use m’inscrire after je voudrais.

vocabulary.example: Quel est le niveau de ce cours ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: What level is this course?
vocabulary.note: A course level describes the class, not a guarantee of your proficiency.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am a beginner in French.
vocabulary.note: Adjective: débutante for a woman. A beginner can also say je débute.

vocabulary.example: Je cherche un cours en ligne.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am looking for an online course.
vocabulary.note: Fixed phrase; no article after en.

vocabulary.example: Je préfère un cours en présentiel.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I prefer an in-person class.
vocabulary.note: Common course information wording; en ligne is the contrasting format.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am listening to the teacher.
vocabulary.note: Écouter takes a direct object: écouter la professeure, without à.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: What page are we on?
vocabulary.note: À la page dix means on page ten.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I underline the verb.
vocabulary.note: Regular -er verb; useful as a classroom instruction.

vocabulary.example: Je recopie la phrase dans mon cahier.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I copy the sentence into my notebook.
vocabulary.note: Here copy written text, rather than make a photocopy.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: We are going to work in pairs.
vocabulary.note: À deux means with two people in the group.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am at work.
vocabulary.note: Au travail means at work or to work.

vocabulary.example: Mon bureau est au premier étage.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: My office is on the first floor.
vocabulary.note: Context distinguishes a room from a desk.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: This is my colleague Sami.
vocabulary.note: Un collègue for a man; une collègue for a woman.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Our team works here.
vocabulary.note: Use notre for our before a singular noun.

vocabulary.example: La responsable arrive à neuf heures.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The person in charge arrives at nine.
vocabulary.note: La responsable for a woman; le responsable for a man. Neutral workplace wording.

vocabulary.example: La formation est dans cette salle.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The training session is in this room.
vocabulary.note: Commonly a shared room, not a bedroom.

vocabulary.example: Le cours commence à dix heures.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The class starts at ten.
vocabulary.note: Un cours has a final s even in the singular.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The teacher writes on the board.
vocabulary.note: Un professeur for a man.

vocabulary.example: Je note les mots dans mon cahier.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I write the words in my notebook.
vocabulary.note: A paper exercise book.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Do you have a pen?
vocabulary.note: Common shortened form of stylographe.

vocabulary.example: Je fais cet exercice avec vous.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am doing this exercise with you.
vocabulary.note: Cet before a masculine noun beginning with a vowel.

vocabulary.example: Je veux apprendre le français au travail.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I want to learn French at work.
vocabulary.note: Irregular verb; j’apprends means I learn or I am learning.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Can you help me print?
vocabulary.note: Regular -er verb; m’ means me before a vowel.

vocabulary.example: Voici le document pour la réunion.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Here is the document for the meeting.
vocabulary.note: Digital or on paper.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I need to print this page.
vocabulary.note: Regular -er verb; common for paper copies.

vocabulary.example: Le fichier est sur mon ordinateur.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The file is on my computer.
vocabulary.note: Ordinateur does not mean calculator.

vocabulary.example: Je ne comprends pas cette phrase.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I do not understand this sentence.
vocabulary.note: Irregular verb; je comprends has a silent final s.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I ask at reception.
vocabulary.note: L’ replaces le before a vowel. Here the place to ask for information.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am looking for counter three.
vocabulary.note: Used in public services and transport.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I would like this form.
vocabulary.note: Paper or digital.

vocabulary.example: J’ai besoin d’aide pour ce formulaire.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I need help with this form.
vocabulary.note: Besoin d’aide has no article in this general expression.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Can I wait here?
vocabulary.note: Attendre takes a person or thing directly: attendre mon tour, wait for my turn.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Here is my address.
vocabulary.note: Mon is used before its vowel sound.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: What is your postcode?
vocabulary.note: French postcodes have five digits.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Here is my phone number.
vocabulary.note: For a contact number, not the mathematical concept nombre.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I would like to send this letter.
vocabulary.note: Here a posted message, not an alphabet letter.

vocabulary.example: Quel timbre faut-il pour cette lettre ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Which stamp do I need for this letter?
vocabulary.note: Ask staff which stamp is suitable.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I would like to post this letter.
vocabulary.note: Poster une lettre means put a letter in the post. Envoyer is the broader verb to send.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I have come to collect a parcel.
vocabulary.note: Final s is silent and remains in the singular.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The recipient lives in Lille.
vocabulary.note: Le destinataire for a man or an unspecified person; la destinataire for a woman.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: What is your occupation?
vocabulary.note: A kind of work or profession, rather than a particular vacancy.

vocabulary.example: Je cherche un emploi à Nantes.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am looking for a job in Nantes.
vocabulary.note: Un emploi is a job; le travail can refer to work in general.

vocabulary.example: Je voudrais chercher un emploi ici.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I would like to look for a job here.
vocabulary.note: Chercher takes a direct object, without pour.

vocabulary.example: Je cherche un emploi à temps plein.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am looking for a full-time job.
vocabulary.note: Fixed phrase used to describe a work schedule; no specific hours are implied here.

vocabulary.example: Je préfère travailler à temps partiel.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I prefer to work part-time.
vocabulary.note: Fixed phrase; ask about the actual hours for a particular job.

vocabulary.example: Je voudrais travailler dans un magasin.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I would like to work in a shop.
vocabulary.note: Regular -er verb: je travaille.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Can you speak more slowly?
vocabulary.note: Adverb; plus lentement means more slowly.

vocabulary.example: Je comprends un peu le français.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I understand a little French.
vocabulary.note: Fixed expression; un peu de before an uncountable noun.

vocabulary.example: Je n’ai pas compris votre question.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I did not understand your question.
vocabulary.note: A ready-to-use past-tense phrase. Keep ne… pas around ai; compris stays unchanged here.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: May I ask a question?
vocabulary.note: Poser une question means ask a question.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Thank you for your answer.
vocabulary.note: Répondre is the verb to answer.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Sorry, I did not understand.
vocabulary.note: Désolée for a feminine speaker; excusez-moi is useful to get attention.

vocabulary.example: Je suis nouvelle dans le quartier.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am new to the neighbourhood.
vocabulary.note: A part of a town or city.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I have just arrived in Nantes.
vocabulary.note: Regular -er verb; venir de + infinitive expresses the recent past.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Do you know the neighbourhood?
vocabulary.note: Use for familiarity with people or places; savoir is used for knowing a fact or how to do something.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I would like to meet my neighbours.
vocabulary.note: Regular -er verb; takes a direct object.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am new here.
vocabulary.note: Adjective: nouvelle for feminine; nouvel before a masculine vowel sound.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Welcome to the neighbourhood!
vocabulary.note: Greeting expression; bienvenue keeps this ending when welcoming anyone.

vocabulary.example: Quelle est la date du cours ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: What is the date of the class?
vocabulary.note: A calendar date, not usually a romantic date.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am staying here for a month.
vocabulary.note: Written form unchanged in the plural.

vocabulary.example: Je reste une année en France.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am staying in France for a year.
vocabulary.note: Année often presents a year as a duration or lived period.

vocabulary.example: La visite est le premier juin.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The visit is on the first of June.
vocabulary.note: For dates use premier for 1, then ordinary numbers: le deux.

vocabulary.example: Je peux venir la semaine prochaine.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I can come next week.
vocabulary.note: Use la, but no extra preposition for this time phrase.

vocabulary.example: Je me lève à sept heures.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I get up at seven.
vocabulary.note: Reflexive verb; je me lève, vous vous levez.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I have a shower in the morning.
vocabulary.note: Reflexive verb; keep me with je.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I have breakfast.
vocabulary.note: Petit-déjeuner with a hyphen is also an accepted spelling.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I leave at eight.
vocabulary.note: Irregular verb; je pars, nous partons.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I get home around six p.m.
vocabulary.note: Here return home; vers makes the time approximate.

vocabulary.example: Je me couche à vingt-trois heures.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I go to bed at eleven p.m.
vocabulary.note: Reflexive verb; je me couche, vous vous couchez.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: First, I prepare the meal.
vocabulary.note: Sequence marker; keep its apostrophe.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Then I tidy the kitchen.
vocabulary.note: Sequence marker; often at the start of a clause.

vocabulary.example: Je fais les courses avant midi.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I do the shopping before noon.
vocabulary.note: Here before a time; avant de + infinitive for before doing something.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I walk after the meal.
vocabulary.note: Preposition here; keep the grave accent.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Usually, I come home early.
vocabulary.note: Useful for describing your normal routine.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Sometimes I work on Saturdays.
vocabulary.note: Adverb; no change for gender or number.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: It is near the library.
vocabulary.note: Keep de before the place.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The police station is far from here.
vocabulary.note: De becomes d’ before ici.

vocabulary.example: La banque est au bout de la rue.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The bank is at the end of the street.
vocabulary.note: Use for an end point in space here.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Continue as far as the square.
vocabulary.note: Jusqu’à + le becomes jusqu’au.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: You need to turn back.
vocabulary.note: A fixed phrase; here in a walking route.

vocabulary.target: à combien de minutes à pied ?
vocabulary.meaning: how many minutes away on foot?
vocabulary.example: La mairie est à combien de minutes à pied ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: How many minutes away on foot is the town hall?
vocabulary.note: Everyday spoken way to check walking time.

vocabulary.example: Le départ est à neuf heures.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Departure is at nine o’clock.
Arrival is scheduled for noon.

vocabulary.meaning: a connection; a change of service
vocabulary.example: Il y a une correspondance à Tours.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: There is a change at Tours.

vocabulary.example: Ce train est direct pour Lyon ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Is this train direct to Lyon?
vocabulary.note: Adjective; feminine directe. Direct does not necessarily mean non-stop.

vocabulary.example: Je dois changer de train à Tours.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I need to change trains at Tours.
vocabulary.note: No article between changer de and train in this expression.

vocabulary.example: Je dois descendre au prochain arrêt.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I need to get off at the next stop.
vocabulary.note: Infinitive verb. Descendre du bus means get off the bus.

vocabulary.example: Je vérifie les horaires des trains.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am checking the train times.
vocabulary.note: Here the scheduled departure or arrival times of a transport service. Les horaires des trains means the train timetable.

vocabulary.example: Le train a vingt minutes de retard.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The train is twenty minutes late.
vocabulary.note: Avoir du retard means to be delayed.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: My train is cancelled.
vocabulary.note: Adjective: annulé with train, annulée with a feminine noun.

vocabulary.example: Où part le car de remplacement ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Where does the replacement coach leave from?
vocabulary.note: Car usually means a coach, not a private car.

vocabulary.example: Le prochain bus arrive dans combien de temps ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: How long until the next bus arrives?
vocabulary.note: Ask how long until an event, rather than the clock time.

vocabulary.example: Le prochain arrive dans dix minutes.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The next one arrives in ten minutes.
vocabulary.note: Masculine form referring back to a train, bus or other masculine noun; feminine la prochaine.

vocabulary.example: Il y a un autre itinéraire ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Is there another route?
vocabulary.note: Itinéraire means a route.

vocabulary.example: Je voudrais un renseignement sur les cars.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I would like some information about the coaches.
vocabulary.note: Des renseignements means information.

vocabulary.example: Je voudrais un sandwich au fromage.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I would like a cheese sandwich.
Is this a vegetable quiche?
vocabulary.note: Fillings vary; ask if ingredients matter.

vocabulary.example: Une part de quiche, s’il vous plaît.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: A slice of quiche, please.
vocabulary.note: Used for a portion cut from a larger food.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Does the set lunch deal include a drink?
vocabulary.note: Contents depend on the bakery.

vocabulary.example: C’est à emporter, s’il vous plaît.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: It’s to take away, please.
vocabulary.note: Service phrase. Sur place means to eat on the premises.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Can you heat up my quiche?
vocabulary.note: Infinitive verb. Use after pouvez in a request.

vocabulary.example: Un gâteau pour six personnes, s’il vous plaît.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: A cake for six people, please.
vocabulary.note: Plural: des gâteaux.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I’m here to collect my order.

vocabulary.example: Je voudrais commander un gâteau pour samedi.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I would like to order a cake for Saturday.
vocabulary.note: Infinitive verb. Here ordering ahead rather than asking at the counter.

vocabulary.example: Je peux venir chercher le gâteau demain ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Can I come and collect the cake tomorrow?
vocabulary.note: Verb phrase; venir describes coming to the bakery.

vocabulary.example: Des croissants ? Il n’y en a plus.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Croissants? There are none left.
vocabulary.note: Useful stock phrase. Here plus means no more; its final s is silent.

vocabulary.example: Le rayon des surgelés est au fond.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The frozen-food section is at the back.
vocabulary.note: Rayon means a department or product section here.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Is this checkout open?

vocabulary.example: Je prends un panier pour mes courses.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I’m taking a basket for my shopping.
Where are the frozen foods?

vocabulary.example: Les pâtes sont au fond du magasin.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The pasta is at the back of the shop.
vocabulary.note: Location phrase; au combines à and le.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Where are the shopping trolleys?
The price is on the label.
These yogurts are on special offer.
vocabulary.note: The everyday phrase is en promotion.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am going to check the numbers.
vocabulary.note: Regular -er verb; use for checking accuracy.

vocabulary.example: Il manque un euro dans la monnaie.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: One euro is missing from the change.
vocabulary.note: Here money returned after paying.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I’m going to pay in cash.
vocabulary.note: Payment phrase.

vocabulary.example: Il y a une erreur sur mon ticket.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: There is a mistake on my receipt.
vocabulary.note: Polite phrase for reporting a mistake.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: This salad contains an egg.
vocabulary.note: Plural: des œufs.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Does this sauce contain eggs?
vocabulary.note: Infinitive: contenir. Useful present form: contient.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The sauce contains eggs.

vocabulary.example: Je voudrais la salade sans sauce.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I would like the salad without sauce.
vocabulary.note: Preposition. Usually no article after sans when naming an omitted ingredient.

vocabulary.example: Vous pouvez mettre la sauce à part ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Can you put the sauce on the side?
vocabulary.note: Food-service phrase. This request alone does not communicate an allergy.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Does this soup contain milk?
vocabulary.note: Du describes an unspecified amount.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I’m missing a fork.

vocabulary.example: Je peux avoir une autre serviette ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Can I have another napkin?
vocabulary.note: At a table this is a napkin; elsewhere it can mean a towel.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I’m paying by bank card.
vocabulary.note: Not the restaurant menu.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Can we pay separately?
vocabulary.note: Adverb. Ask whether the restaurant can split payment.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Can I have a receipt?
vocabulary.note: Here a payment receipt, not a transport ticket.

vocabulary.example: Je peux avoir un autre couteau ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Can I have another knife?
vocabulary.note: Plural: des couteaux.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Where is the fitting room?
Can I try on this jacket?
vocabulary.note: Infinitive verb. Also means to try in other contexts.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: This jacket fits me well.
These trousers are too tight.
vocabulary.note: Adjective phrase; feminine trop serrée.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The sleeves are too long.
vocabulary.note: Adjective forms: long, longue, longs, longues.

vocabulary.meaning: it fits me; it suits me
vocabulary.example: Ça me va bien. Je le prends.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: It fits me well. I’ll take it.
vocabulary.note: Everyday phrase for fit or appearance; the context identifies which meaning is intended.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Is an exchange possible?
vocabulary.note: Ask about the shop’s conditions.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I would like a refund.
vocabulary.note: This phrase does not establish a right to a refund.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Here is the till receipt.
vocabulary.note: A till receipt; keep it if you may need to return an item. Conditions vary by shop and situation.

vocabulary.example: Il y a un défaut sur la manche.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: There is a defect on the sleeve.
I would like to bring this jumper back.
vocabulary.note: Infinitive verb; bringing an item back to the shop.

vocabulary.meaning: it does not fit me; it does not suit me
vocabulary.example: Ce pantalon, ça ne me va pas.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: These trousers don’t fit me.
vocabulary.note: Everyday phrase. Here the context is an unsuitable fit.

vocabulary.example: Le loyer est de huit cents euros.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The rent is eight hundred euros.
Are service charges included?
vocabulary.note: Ask what is included; arrangements vary.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I would like to read the tenancy agreement.
vocabulary.note: Plural: des baux.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I’m going to call the landlord.
vocabulary.note: Feminine: la propriétaire. Here the owner who rents out the home; not a statement about legal responsibilities.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I’m going to move in on Saturday.
vocabulary.note: One move into a new home; déménager means move home.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The flat is furnished.
vocabulary.note: Adjective: meublé for appartement; meublée with a feminine noun.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I’m the new tenant.
vocabulary.note: Feminine: une locataire.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The heating is not working.

vocabulary.example: Il y a une fuite sous l’évier.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: There is a leak under the kitchen sink.

vocabulary.example: Le robinet de la cuisine coule.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The kitchen tap is leaking.
The window doesn’t close properly.

vocabulary.meaning: to arrange for someone to come
vocabulary.example: Vous pouvez faire venir quelqu’un demain ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Can you arrange for someone to come tomorrow?
vocabulary.note: Learn as a request chunk; someone else will come to help.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The washing machine has broken down.
vocabulary.note: Fixed phrase used for equipment that is not working.

vocabulary.example: La réparation est prévue demain matin.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The repair is scheduled for tomorrow morning.
Shall we meet on Sunday instead?
vocabulary.note: Keep the circumflex; plus tôt, two words, means earlier.

vocabulary.example: S’il pleut, on va au musée.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: If it rains, we will go to the museum.
vocabulary.note: Si becomes s’ before il and ils; for a realistic future condition, use the present after si.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: We are planning an outing on Saturday.
vocabulary.note: Irregular verb; je prévois, nous prévoyons.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The outing is cancelled.
vocabulary.note: Here a leisure outing, not an exit.

vocabulary.example: Le musée ferme à dix-huit heures.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The museum closes at six p.m.
vocabulary.note: Despite its ending in -ée, use un musée.

vocabulary.meaning: to postpone / move to a later date
vocabulary.example: On peut reporter la promenade à dimanche.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: We can postpone the walk until Sunday.
vocabulary.note: Regular -er verb; here change a plan to a later time.

vocabulary.example: On se retrouve devant le cinéma.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: We will meet in front of the cinema.
vocabulary.note: Here a planned meeting; on takes se.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Can we set a time?
vocabulary.note: Une heure is feminine; here an agreed meeting time.

vocabulary.example: La place est notre lieu de rendez-vous.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The square is our meeting place.
vocabulary.note: Lieu is masculine; plural lieux.

vocabulary.example: À quelle heure on se retrouve ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: What time are we meeting?
vocabulary.note: Everyday spoken question; quelle agrees with heure.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: We can check together.
vocabulary.note: Adverb; no plural ending. On often means we in spoken French.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am going to let the teacher know.
vocabulary.note: Prévenir quelqu’un takes a direct object, without à.

vocabulary.meaning: in the end / as it turns out
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: As it turns out, I am free on Saturday.
vocabulary.note: Often introduces a changed decision or situation.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I need to cancel my appointment.
vocabulary.note: Regular -er verb; annuler un rendez-vous means cancel an appointment.

vocabulary.example: Je confirme pour vendredi à dix heures.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I confirm Friday at ten.
vocabulary.note: Regular -er verb; confirmer un rendez-vous means confirm an appointment.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: We are going to change plans.
vocabulary.note: Programme here means a plan for activities, not software.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I have been in pain since yesterday.
vocabulary.note: Use with a starting point or duration for a situation still continuing.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I cough mainly at night.
vocabulary.note: Regular -er verb; describe what you notice, without diagnosing it.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The pain is here.
vocabulary.note: A more precise noun than the general expression avoir mal.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: It started on Monday.
vocabulary.note: Ça a commencé is a useful spoken past-tense phrase.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: It often happens in the evening.
vocabulary.note: Adverb of frequency; no gender or plural ending.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Can you repeat the question?
vocabulary.note: Polite request; useful if health vocabulary is unfamiliar.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I would like to reschedule my appointment.
vocabulary.note: Here déplacer means move an appointment to a different time.

vocabulary.meaning: a conflicting commitment / something preventing attendance
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Something has come up on Thursday.
vocabulary.note: A polite general explanation without personal details.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Do you have a time slot on Friday?
vocabulary.note: Common in appointment scheduling.

vocabulary.example: Je suis en retard de dix minutes.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am running ten minutes late.
vocabulary.note: Fixed expression with être; do not add an article.

vocabulary.example: Je fais bouillir l’eau dans une casserole.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I boil the water in a saucepan.

vocabulary.example: Les légumes cuisent dans la poêle.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The vegetables are cooking in the frying pan.
vocabulary.note: Pronounced like poil; here a cooking pan, not un poêle, a stove.

vocabulary.example: Je mets le plat dans le four.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I put the dish in the oven.
