vocabulary.note: Here plat means an oven dish, not the main-course sense.

vocabulary.example: Je fais cuire les légumes dix minutes.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I cook the vegetables for ten minutes.
vocabulary.note: Faire cuire + food: causing the food to cook. Je fais cuire; the food itself cuit.

vocabulary.meaning: to bring to the boil; to boil
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Can you boil the water?
vocabulary.note: Useful fixed verb phrase. Bouillir stays in the infinitive after faire.

vocabulary.example: Faites cuire la soupe à feu doux.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Cook the soup over a low heat.
vocabulary.note: A recipe instruction; doux describes feu, a masculine noun.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I’m going to serve the soup.
vocabulary.note: Present: je sers. Infinitive after vais: servir.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I let the soup cool.
vocabulary.note: Laisser + infinitive: let something happen. This phrase does not specify storage timing.

vocabulary.example: Où est le couvercle de cette boîte ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Where is the lid for this container?

vocabulary.example: Je mets les légumes dans une boîte.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I put the vegetables in a container.
vocabulary.note: Here a food-storage container.

vocabulary.example: Tu peux mettre cette boîte au réfrigérateur ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Can you put this container in the refrigerator?
vocabulary.note: Au combines à and le. Frigo is common in conversation.

vocabulary.example: On garde les restes pour demain ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Shall we keep the leftovers for tomorrow?
vocabulary.note: Plural for leftover food.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The connection is slow.
vocabulary.note: Here an internet connection.

vocabulary.example: Est-ce qu’il y a le Wi-Fi ici ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Is there Wi-Fi here?
vocabulary.note: Masculine; also written wifi.

vocabulary.example: Quel est le nom du réseau ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: What is the network called?
vocabulary.note: Plural réseaux.

vocabulary.example: Je n’arrive pas à me connecter.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I cannot manage to log in.
vocabulary.note: Reflexive verb; je me connecte, vous vous connectez.

vocabulary.example: Je me déconnecte après mon travail.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I log out after my work.
vocabulary.note: For an account or a connection; the reflexive pronoun is needed.

vocabulary.example: Je télécharge le document sur mon téléphone.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am downloading the document onto my phone.
vocabulary.note: Here transfer a file onto your device.

vocabulary.example: Je vais mettre le document en ligne.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am going to upload the document.
vocabulary.note: Useful present forms: je mets, nous mettons.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Can you send me the link?
vocabulary.note: Here a clickable web link.

vocabulary.example: Le formulaire est en pièce jointe.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The form is attached.
vocabulary.note: A file attached to an email.

vocabulary.meaning: to open a file or app
vocabulary.example: Je ne peux pas ouvrir ce fichier.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I cannot open this file.
vocabulary.note: Digital action: open a file, message or app.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am going to save the file.
vocabulary.note: Here save a file, rather than record a voice.

vocabulary.example: Il y a du bruit dans le couloir.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: There is noise in the corridor.
vocabulary.note: Un bruit can mean one particular sound.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The air conditioning is not working.
vocabulary.note: La clim is a common informal shortening.

vocabulary.example: Il n’y a pas d’eau chaude.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: There is no hot water.
vocabulary.note: Chaude agrees with feminine eau. After pas, de l’ becomes d’.

vocabulary.example: Il manque une serviette dans la chambre.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: A towel is missing from the room.
vocabulary.note: Il manque + the missing item; il stays singular in this impersonal expression.

vocabulary.example: Est-ce que je peux changer de chambre ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Can I change rooms?
vocabulary.note: No article between de and chambre in this expression.

vocabulary.example: La douche ne fonctionne pas. Quelqu’un peut venir ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The shower is not working. Can someone come?
vocabulary.note: A useful spoken request. Use vous with reception staff.

vocabulary.example: À quelle heure faut-il libérer la chambre ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: What time must the room be vacated?
vocabulary.note: A common formal hotel expression; staff may also say quitter la chambre.

vocabulary.example: Je peux laisser mes bagages ici ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Can I leave my luggage here?
vocabulary.note: Usually plural; one item is un bagage.

vocabulary.example: Je voudrais laisser mes bagages jusqu’à midi.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I would like to leave my luggage until noon.
vocabulary.note: Ask whether storage is available; mes means my with a plural noun.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Can I stay until noon?
vocabulary.note: Before les, jusqu’à becomes jusqu’aux: jusqu’aux vacances.

vocabulary.example: Je peux avoir une facture à mon nom ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Can I have an invoice in my name?
vocabulary.note: More formal than a payment receipt; useful for accommodation costs.

vocabulary.example: Il y a un supplément pour les bagages ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Is there an extra charge for the luggage?
vocabulary.note: Ask before agreeing to an optional service.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The next session is on Thursday.
vocabulary.note: One scheduled meeting within a course.

vocabulary.example: Mon emploi du temps a changé.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: My timetable has changed.
vocabulary.note: A fixed noun phrase; emploi here does not mean a job.

vocabulary.example: Quelle est la durée du cours ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: How long is the class?
vocabulary.note: Ask combien de temps dure le cours ? as another natural question.

vocabulary.example: Il y a une pause à onze heures.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: There is a break at eleven.
vocabulary.note: Faire une pause means take a break.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I will be absent on Thursday.
vocabulary.note: Absente for a woman. Je serai is a useful future form of être.

vocabulary.example: Quels sont les devoirs pour lundi ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: What is the homework for Monday?
vocabulary.note: Usually plural for school or course homework. Un devoir can mean one assignment.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am going to review the verbs.
vocabulary.note: In learning, review material you have already studied.

vocabulary.example: Je m’entraîne dix minutes par jour.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I practise for ten minutes a day.
vocabulary.note: Reflexive verb: je m’entraîne. S’entrainer without the circumflex is also accepted spelling.

vocabulary.meaning: to look up / look for a word
vocabulary.example: Je cherche un mot dans le dictionnaire.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am looking up a word in the dictionary.
vocabulary.note: Dans le dictionnaire makes it clear that you are looking the word up.

vocabulary.example: Je vérifie la traduction de ce mot.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I check the translation of this word.
vocabulary.note: La traduction de + the original word or phrase.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: This dictionary gives examples.
vocabulary.note: Dans un dictionnaire means in a dictionary.

vocabulary.example: Je fais des progrès en français.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am making progress in French.
vocabulary.note: Faire des progrès is the usual expression. Progrès keeps its final s in the singular too.

vocabulary.example: J’ai fait une erreur dans cette phrase.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I made a mistake in this sentence.
vocabulary.note: Une erreur is feminine; j’ai fait is a useful past form.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I managed to finish the exercise.
vocabulary.note: Réussir à + infinitive means manage to do something; réussir un exercice means complete an exercise successfully.

vocabulary.example: Mon objectif est de parler au téléphone.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: My goal is to speak on the phone.
vocabulary.note: Un objectif de travail here is a learning goal, not proof of proficiency.

vocabulary.example: J’ai du mal à comprendre les nombres.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I find it difficult to understand numbers.
vocabulary.note: Follow à with an infinitive. This means difficulty, unlike avoir mal à for physical pain.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I work at my own pace.
vocabulary.note: Change son to mon with je: à mon rythme.

vocabulary.example: La réunion commence à quatorze heures.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The meeting starts at two p.m.
vocabulary.note: Workplace sense.

vocabulary.example: Mon horaire de travail change lundi.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: My work schedule changes on Monday.
vocabulary.note: Here the organisation of working hours. Les horaires de travail is the usual plural phrase for working hours; the noun is masculine.

vocabulary.example: Quel est le délai pour répondre ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: How long do we have to reply?
vocabulary.note: A period of time, not always a specific due date.

vocabulary.example: Je commence cette tâche ce matin.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am starting this task this morning.
vocabulary.note: Keep the circumflex: tache without it means a stain.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am going to finish before noon.
vocabulary.note: Regular -er verb; can take an object directly.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: This message is urgent.
vocabulary.note: Adjective: urgente with a feminine noun.

vocabulary.example: Je ne comprends pas la consigne.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I do not understand the instruction.
vocabulary.note: A direction for a task.

vocabulary.example: Il y a un problème dans le document.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: There is a problem in the document.
vocabulary.note: Despite its final e, use un problème.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I suggest looking together.
vocabulary.note: Regular -er verb; proposer de + infinitive for suggesting an action.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: We are looking for a solution.
vocabulary.note: Une solution à un problème.

vocabulary.example: Je peux faire cette démarche en ligne ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Can I complete this procedure online?
vocabulary.note: Here a practical administrative step. Faire une démarche is a useful combination.

vocabulary.example: Il manque une attestation dans mon dossier.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: A certificate is missing from my application file.
vocabulary.note: A document confirming a fact; its purpose depends on the request. This is not the name of one universal form.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Where can I submit my application file?
vocabulary.note: Déposer can mean submit at a desk or through an online service. Un dossier is masculine.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The website is not working.
vocabulary.note: Regular -er verb; use for equipment or services, rather than someone’s job.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: What is the deadline?
vocabulary.note: The last date for an action. Un délai is a period of time allowed, which is a related but different idea.

vocabulary.example: J’ai reçu un accusé de réception.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I received an acknowledgement of receipt.
vocabulary.note: Confirms receipt of a message or application; it does not by itself mean the request was approved. Learn the expression as a whole.

vocabulary.meaning: an application file / set of documents
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Is my application file complete?
vocabulary.note: Here a set of paperwork for a request.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Which supporting document should I bring?
vocabulary.note: Requirements depend on the service, so ask rather than assume.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Your signature is missing.
vocabulary.note: Signer is the verb to sign.

vocabulary.example: Vous pouvez m’aider à remplir ce formulaire ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Can you help me fill in this form?
vocabulary.note: Regular -ir verb; remplir un formulaire means fill in a form.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: A page is missing.
vocabulary.note: Il manque + a noun is a useful impersonal pattern.

vocabulary.example: Vous voulez une copie de ce document ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Would you like a copy of this document?
vocabulary.note: Check the actual service instructions.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: This job advertisement interests me.
vocabulary.note: An advertisement for a job; no hiring promise is implied.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Is the position still available?
vocabulary.note: Here a job position; different from un bureau de poste, a post office.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am sending you my application.
vocabulary.note: Envoyer une candidature means send an application.

vocabulary.example: Je voudrais postuler à ce poste.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I would like to apply for this position.
vocabulary.note: Postuler à un poste is a useful standard pattern.

vocabulary.example: Voici mon CV en pièce jointe.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: My CV is attached.
vocabulary.note: Pronounce the French letter names C and V. CV is short for curriculum vitæ.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Do I need a covering letter?
vocabulary.note: Ask what this particular application needs; requirements vary.

vocabulary.example: J’ai de l’expérience dans la vente.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I have experience in sales.
vocabulary.note: For experience in general, use de l’expérience. Une expérience can be one particular role or experience.

vocabulary.example: Cette compétence est utile pour ce poste.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: This skill is useful for this position.
vocabulary.note: A skill or ability; not a job title.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I have a qualification in cookery.
vocabulary.note: Naming a diploma does not establish its recognition or equivalence.

vocabulary.example: Quelle qualification demandez-vous pour ce poste ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: What qualification do you require for this position?
vocabulary.note: Ask the recruiter what is required; this lesson gives no eligibility advice.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I know how to use a till.
vocabulary.note: Je sais + infinitive describes an ability. Une caisse here means a shop till.

vocabulary.example: Je suis autonome pour cette tâche.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I can do this task independently.
vocabulary.note: Same adjective form for masculine and feminine; say which task you can handle.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I have a job interview on Tuesday.
vocabulary.note: Un entretien d’embauche is the full phrase for a recruitment interview.

vocabulary.example: Je vais me présenter en quelques phrases.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am going to introduce myself in a few sentences.
vocabulary.note: Reflexive verb: je me présente; use me présenter after je vais.

vocabulary.example: Je vais parler de mon parcours.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am going to talk about my background.
vocabulary.note: Here someone’s studies and working life, not a physical route.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: When are you available?
vocabulary.note: Often plural when asking about times someone can work or meet.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am keen to learn.
vocabulary.note: Motivée for a woman; give a concrete example rather than only an adjective.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Can you explain this contract to me?
vocabulary.note: Language for asking a question, not advice on contract terms or rights.

vocabulary.example: Quel est le salaire pour ce poste ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: What is the pay for this position?
vocabulary.note: Ask what a figure refers to; this lesson makes no pay or entitlement claim.

vocabulary.example: Vous souhaitez embaucher quelqu’un pour quand ?
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: When do you want someone to start?
vocabulary.note: The employer embauche; the applicant can say être embauché or embauchée.

vocabulary.meaning: to contact again / get back to
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: When will you get back to me?
vocabulary.note: Direct object: recontacter quelqu’un.

vocabulary.example: Je voudrais lire le contrat avant d’accepter.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I would like to read the contract before accepting.
vocabulary.note: Accepter une offre means accept an offer.

vocabulary.example: Merci, mais je dois refuser cette offre.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Thank you, but I need to decline this offer.
vocabulary.note: A clear, polite refusal can start merci, mais…

vocabulary.example: Le week-end dernier, j’ai visité Lyon.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Last weekend, I visited Lyon.
vocabulary.note: Use le; dernier agrees with masculine week-end.

vocabulary.example: J’ai commencé ce cours la semaine dernière.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I started this class last week.
vocabulary.note: Dernière agrees with feminine semaine.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The day before yesterday, I saw Léa.
vocabulary.note: A single time expression with a hyphen.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I discovered this café recently.
vocabulary.note: An adverb; no gender ending.

vocabulary.example: Ce jour-là, j’ai pris le train.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: That day, I took the train.
vocabulary.note: Refers back to a day already mentioned.

vocabulary.example: Hier soir, j’ai dîné avec des amis.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Last night, I had dinner with friends.
vocabulary.note: The evening of yesterday, not necessarily the overnight period.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Then, I met up with my friends.
vocabulary.note: Links the next action in a sequence.

vocabulary.example: Après, nous avons pris un café.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Afterwards, we had a coffee.
vocabulary.note: Can stand alone or introduce a noun: après la visite.

vocabulary.example: À la fin, nous avons pris une photo.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: At the end, we took a photo.
vocabulary.note: À la fin de la visite means at the end of the visit.

vocabulary.example: Nous avons marché pendant une heure.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: We walked for an hour.
vocabulary.note: Here a bounded duration that ended.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I visited a small museum.
vocabulary.note: Use visiter for a place; rendre visite à for visiting a person.

vocabulary.example: Nous avons découvert un joli jardin.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: We discovered a lovely garden.
vocabulary.note: Past participle découvert.

vocabulary.example: J’ai pris des photos du pont.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I took photos of the bridge.
vocabulary.note: Une photo is feminine; past participle pris.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I tried a local speciality.
vocabulary.note: Here try food; un goûter is a snack.

vocabulary.example: Nous avons passé la journée à Lille.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: We spent the day in Lille.
vocabulary.note: Passer with avoir here means spend time.

vocabulary.meaning: to enjoy / make the most of
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: We made the most of the sunshine.
vocabulary.note: De + le becomes du; not the English sense exploit a person.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: It was a lovely day.
vocabulary.note: Useful background or evaluation chunk; part of the imparfait.

vocabulary.example: Mon premier cours, ça s’est bien passé.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: My first class went well.
vocabulary.note: Learn as a whole phrase for how an event went.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I had a lot of fun.
vocabulary.note: A feminine speaker writes amusée in this example.

vocabulary.example: Je garde un bon souvenir de cette journée.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I have a good memory of that day.
vocabulary.note: Here a memory, not a purchased souvenir.

vocabulary.example: C’était une nouvelle expérience pour moi.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: It was a new experience for me.
vocabulary.note: Here something you lived through, not a scientific experiment.

vocabulary.meaning: to feel like doing it again
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I feel like doing it again.
vocabulary.note: Avoir envie de + dictionary verb.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I lost my keys on Saturday.
vocabulary.note: Past participle perdu.

vocabulary.example: J’ai retrouvé mes clés dans mon sac.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I found my keys in my bag.
vocabulary.note: Here recover something lost; another sense is meet up with someone.

vocabulary.example: J’ai oublié mon téléphone chez moi.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I forgot my phone at home.
vocabulary.note: Oublier quelque chose: no preposition before the thing.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I missed the last bus.
vocabulary.note: Here fail to catch a service; rater le bus is also common.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Fortunately, Léa helped me.
vocabulary.note: Aidée if the person helped is feminine in this written example.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Unfortunately, the museum was closed.
vocabulary.note: Introduces an unwelcome part of the story.

vocabulary.example: Je préfère le train au bus.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I prefer the train to the bus.
vocabulary.note: Préférer A à B; present je préfère.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I love this neighbourhood.
vocabulary.note: Stronger than aimer in everyday speech.

vocabulary.example: Je déteste attendre sous la pluie.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I hate waiting in the rain.
vocabulary.note: A strong preference; use carefully about people.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I feel like walking.
vocabulary.note: Use de before an activity verb; de becomes d’ before a vowel.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I like this idea.
vocabulary.note: The thing is the subject; me marks who likes it.

vocabulary.example: On choisit le café près de la gare.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: We are choosing the café near the station.
vocabulary.note: Regular -ir verb: je choisis, on choisit.

vocabulary.example: À mon avis, ce café est agréable.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: In my opinion, this café is pleasant.
vocabulary.note: Avis is masculine; useful for signalling a personal view.

vocabulary.example: Je pense que le train est plus simple.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I think the train is simpler.
vocabulary.note: Que connects to a complete statement.

vocabulary.example: Je trouve que cette salle est calme.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I find this room quiet.
vocabulary.note: Here express a judgement, not physically find something.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: For me, it is too far.
vocabulary.note: Here gives your own perspective or constraint.

vocabulary.example: Oui, c’est vrai, le trajet est court.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: Yes, that’s true, the journey is short.
vocabulary.note: A simple acknowledgement before agreeing or adding a point.

vocabulary.example: Je ne suis pas d’accord avec toi.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I disagree with you.
vocabulary.note: Avec introduces the person; avec vous for polite address.

vocabulary.example: Ce trajet est plus court que l’autre.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: This journey is shorter than the other one.
vocabulary.note: Put an adjective between plus and que.

vocabulary.example: Ce café est moins cher que l’autre.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: This café is cheaper than the other one.
vocabulary.note: Literally less expensive than.

vocabulary.example: Cette chambre est aussi grande que l’autre.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: This room is as big as the other one.
vocabulary.note: A comparison of equal degree.

vocabulary.example: Ce pain est meilleur que l’autre.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: This bread is better than the other one.
vocabulary.note: Adjective: meilleure, meilleurs, meilleures.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I sleep better here.
vocabulary.note: Adverb; use to describe an action, not a noun.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: We have the same idea.
vocabulary.note: Même agrees with the noun; plural les mêmes.

vocabulary.example: Ce sac est pratique pour les courses.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: This bag is practical for shopping.
vocabulary.note: Same form for masculine and feminine.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: This chair is comfortable.
vocabulary.note: Same form for masculine and feminine.

vocabulary.example: Cette rue est bruyante le soir.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: This street is noisy in the evening.
vocabulary.note: Bruyante with a feminine noun.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am looking for a quiet café.
vocabulary.note: Here a place without much noise or bustle.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: This room is too expensive.
vocabulary.note: Chère with a feminine noun.

vocabulary.example: Le bus est une solution économique.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: The bus is a budget-friendly option.
vocabulary.note: Here low-cost or saving money, not a claim about the economy.

vocabulary.example: Je prends le bus parce qu’il pleut.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am taking the bus because it is raining.
vocabulary.note: Que becomes qu’ before il.

vocabulary.example: Il pleut, donc je prends le bus.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: It is raining, so I am taking the bus.
vocabulary.note: Introduces a result or conclusion.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: It is convenient, but it is expensive.
vocabulary.note: Joins contrasting points.

vocabulary.example: C’est près. Pourtant, le trajet est long.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: It is nearby. Yet the journey is long.
vocabulary.note: Signals an unexpected contrast; use in short familiar situations.

vocabulary.exampleMeaning: It depends on the price.
vocabulary.note: Dépendre de; de + le becomes du.

vocabulary.example: J’hésite entre le bus et le train.
vocabulary.exampleMeaning: I am undecided between the bus and the train.
vocabulary.note: Hésiter entre A et B is useful when comparing two choices.
